text: The 5th Annual Streamy Awards, the fifth installment of the awards honoring streaming television series, took place on September 17, 2015, at the Hollywood Palladium in Hollywood, California. The event was hosted by YouTube stars Grace Helbig and Tyler Oakley and was broadcast live on VH1 while simultaneously livestreamed online, marking the first time the Streamy Awards were televised.[2][3][4] Several new award categories were introduced, including Social Video awards for content on Instagram, Snapchat, and Vine, subject categories such as Lifestyle and Documentary or Investigative, and Breakout Creator and Breakthrough Artist to recognize emerging creators.[5] Nominees were announced on August 12, 2015,[9][10] with finalists for the Audience Choice Award categories revealed on September 3.[11][12] On September 14, 35 of the award categories were unveiled during the Official Streamys Nominee Reception at the YouTube Space LA,[13] while the remaining nine "marquee categories" were announced during the main ceremony on September 17.[3][14] Winners were selected by the Streamys Blue Ribbon Panel, except for the Audience Choice awards, which were determined by public vote.[5] Rae Votta of The Daily Dot highlighted the unique and creative video segments introducing each award category, produced by online content creators, and noted that the strict runtime due to the televised format improved the show's flow compared to prior years.[3] The musical performances received positive reviews, with Future's performance of "March Madness" being particularly praised by writers from Spin, Vulture, MTV News, and Vice,[6][16][17][18] and Hailee Steinfeld's performance receiving acclaim from Teen Vogue.[19] Votta described the performances as "flashy and impressive" but felt they were disconnected from YouTube and online content creation.[3] Deepa Lakshmin of MTV News lauded Lilly Singh's acceptance speech, in which she credited Google and YouTube for featuring a brown girl on a billboard, calling it "badass" and especially meaningful for Indian fans of Singh's.[20] Social media reception was overwhelmingly positive, with analysis by social TV platform Canvs—using Nielsen Twitter TV ratings—showing that 41.5% of reaction tweets expressed "love" and 16.2% expressed "congrats."[1] The show was also recognized as the leading social non-sports program on television on the day it aired.[21]
